correspondence.component_scope: headward setting and western upper leg
correspondence.finding: SINIT's Dulce Nombre map shows the northern municipal drainage around El Zapote, El Prado de la Cruz and El Limón joining and continuing north, marked Chamelecon Alta in the sub-basin-drainage legend. Abrego Suárez's original regional maps connect the western headward leg to the northeast-running Chamelecón corridor. The COPECO reproduction independently locates this western leg west of La Entrada.
correspondence.correspondence: observed
correspondence.limits: Ordinary headward/corridor correspondence only. The municipal drainage category is not promoted to an official headwater hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: upper and middle mountain corridor to Puente Chamelecón
correspondence.finding: The original UNAH regional river maps show the main northeastward then eastward corridor and its mountain tributary junctions. The detailed El Tablón–Puente Chamelecón map follows the selected bend and mountain exit. Its accompanying study distinguishes broad valley bottoms near El Tablón from a narrower mountain passage before entry to the Sula Valley. Tributary branches remain separately mapped and unnamed here.
correspondence.correspondence: observed

correspondence.component_scope: Sula Valley and La Lima connections
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor passes through the mapped Chamelecón approach to La Lima and turns north through the western Sula floodplain. The original UNAH detail shows the river separately from the Chotepe/Filopo and Maya flood-relief channels. JICA and the attributed CEDVS map continue the river north past the Choloma connection and distinguish older and engineered lower channels.
correspondence.correspondence: observed

correspondence.component_scope: lower older river, coastal junction and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The hydraulic map traces the older Chamelecón route west of the straighter Chambers Canal, then its northeastward coastal reach into the shared outlet connection. The terminal opens to Mar Caribe east of Puerto Cortés and Laguna de Alvarado; the Ulúa has a distinct outlet farther east. JICA's coastal view supplies the receiving-shore setting.
correspondence.correspondence: observed

correspondence.component_scope: material lakes, reservoirs and off-route channels
correspondence.finding: The inspected regional and lower-river maps do not require the selected mainstem to traverse Lago de Yojoa, Laguna de Alvarado or the separately mapped floodplain lakes. Flood-relief canals and the nearby Ulúa are distinguished from the selected river corridor. No unobserved lake or reservoir connector is invoked.
correspondence.correspondence: observed at corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Unnamed headward lake-and-stream branch
correspondence.finding: The northern part of Miertsching Lake sheet depicts the selected headward setting as an upland lake-and-stream branch west/southwest of Souter Lake. The initial small lake/stream reaches join a larger irregular lake and continue southeast through connected small lakes. Nearby western drainage is separately drawn. No headwater hydronym is established.
correspondence.correspondence: Headward setting and generalized drainage correspondence read.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward feeder and northward lake chain
correspondence.finding: The same sheet shows the feeder continuing southeast to an enlarged water passage, then joining the north-trending chain of elongated lakes and channels. Side streams enter this corridor; the connected waterway turns northeast and north through rapids and lake expansions toward Souter Lake. These are actual mapped water links rather than a basin-membership inference.
correspondence.correspondence: Selected feeder-to-main lake chain read.

correspondence.component_scope: Souter Lake and material inflow junctions
correspondence.finding: Miertsching Lake and Committee Bay sheets together depict the southern and central/eastern arms of Souter Lake. The selected southwestern lake chain enters the lake from the south. The lake also receives a separate northern river arm labeled Ajaqutalik and other northern tributary/lake arms. The selected continuation crosses the connected lake arms toward its east end.
correspondence.correspondence: Lake passages, major inflow relationships and eastward continuation read.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lake outlet and southeastward Ajaqutalik reach
correspondence.finding: The east end of Souter Lake continues into the Ajaqutalik River at the western edge of Hall Lake sheet. The river crosses south into Barrow River sheet, where its labeled valley runs southeast and receives side streams before turning north. The adjacent-sheet waterway continuity is visible on the original maps.
correspondence.correspondence: Souter outlet, cross-sheet southeastward river and principal turn read.

correspondence.component_scope: Sanguaq Bend and lower north/northeast valley
correspondence.finding: Hall Lake sheet shows the river returning north from the southern sheet through Sanguaq Bend and continuing northeast along a broad incised valley. Tributaries entering from the west and east and locally divided river passages are visible. The downstream Ajaqutalik label follows this selected corridor toward the coastal lowland.
correspondence.correspondence: Middle/lower route and material tributary junctions read.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal at Roche Bay
correspondence.finding: The same original map shows the Ajaqutalik turning east across the lower coastal corridor and north into the southwestern Roche Bay shore. The river mouth is distinct from the other bay tributaries and from the Hall Lake–Ikerasak system farther north. Roche Bay is depicted within the larger Foxe Basin coastal setting.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal waterway and receiving coast read.

correspondence.component_scope: Bounded primary prose corroboration
correspondence.finding: Hall Lake sheet fisheries notes M2, D3 and D4 independently discuss the lower Ajaqutalik and explicitly place its mouth in Roche Bay. Their fish-movement and near-mouth fishing descriptions are historical context only; they are not used to extend the hydronym over Souter Lake or the selected unnamed headwater branch.
correspondence.correspondence: Primary marginal prose; separate from map correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward tributary and upper Selawik junction
correspondence.finding: The selected beginning occupies a small western tributary/fork within the upper valley. That channel joins the separately labelled Selawik River, which approaches from farther south. The selection then follows the northward upper river and its turn west. The map shows the tributary, junction and surrounding valley throughout.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected interval observed in original primary cartography at generalized corridor scale; no source or connector-view gap.
correspondence.name_scope: The small selected headward tributary remains unnamed. The selected start is not asserted to be the official source of Selawik River.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward upper and middle Selawik corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection proceeds west with the repeatedly labelled Selawik River valley, from the upland reach into increasingly meandering lowland channel and adjacent lake country. Northern Kiliovilik Creek and southern tributary valleys remain separate lateral features. The full reach to the western bend is covered.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected interval observed in original primary cartography at generalized corridor scale; no source or connector-view gap.
correspondence.name_scope: Selawik River is supported for this main-channel corridor; tributary labels are not propagated onto it.

correspondence.component_scope: Tagagawik and Kugarak junction sequence
correspondence.finding: The western portion enters the Tagagawik junction setting and follows the Selawik corridor northward toward the Kugarak and Kawichiark junction area, then turns west into the lower river. The original shows the meanders, tributary arms, adjacent lakes and intervening floodplain.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected interval observed in original primary cartography at generalized corridor scale; no source or connector-view gap.
correspondence.name_scope: The three other river names describe observed junction context, not selected-route aliases. Generalized model chords across meanders are not treated as exact channel banks.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Selawik westward corridor
correspondence.finding: The second fragment continues west in the broad labelled Selawik River corridor through the lake-rich plain. The mapped river meanders widely, while the selected line is generalized. The larger nearby lakes remain distinct waterbodies.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected interval observed in original primary cartography at generalized corridor scale; no source or connector-view gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Throat River departure and Inland Lake approach
correspondence.finding: At the downstream part of the second fragment, the selected route leaves the main Selawik corridor that continues toward Selawik village. It follows the southwesterly Throat River connector beside the Cleveland Lakes setting toward the northern/western side of Inland Lake. The original map and the independent catalogue distinguish Throat River from Selawik River.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected interval observed in original primary cartography at generalized corridor scale; no source or connector-view gap.
correspondence.name_scope: This named connector and lake approach are separate component scopes. Fox River is not the selected connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Inland Lake margin and northward lake/low-ground traverse
correspondence.finding: The third fragment turns away from the Inland Lake margin and runs north across a succession of separately mapped small lakes, wet patches and intervening low ground west of the principal Selawik channel. The whole traverse is visible. Several intervals do not follow a mapped continuous channel; the selected line is not assigned a river hydronym across those lake and land passages.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected interval observed in original primary cartography at generalized corridor scale; no source or connector-view gap.
correspondence.name_scope: Small-lake names remain null. This is observed composite geography rather than an unseen connector. No year-round surface-flow connection, disconnection under every condition, or cause of the model routing is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Kungsugrug and Selawik distributary return
correspondence.finding: Farther north, the selected route meets the mapped Kungsugrug River corridor and reaches a labelled Selawik River distributary. It then bends southwest through the delta branch-and-island setting. The distinct Kungsugrug channel and nearby lake passages remain distinguishable in the original source.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected interval observed in original primary cartography at generalized corridor scale; no source or connector-view gap.
correspondence.name_scope: The names are retained at their local channels. Their presence does not establish a hydronym for the intervening lake/low-ground traverse.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual western delta and lakeshore terminal
correspondence.finding: The final portion lies at the western Selawik delta margin, beside channels opening toward Selawik Lake. The selected last extension crosses a low coastal/island strip and reaches small shore-adjacent water rather than establishing a named river mouth at that exact endpoint. The nearby lake and delta context is fully observed.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire selected interval observed in original primary cartography at generalized corridor scale; no source or connector-view gap.
correspondence.name_scope: Selawik Lake is the broader receiving-water context, supported by the independent FWS prose. The exact terminal small-waterbody name is unknown. Retained terminal class sea is model metadata and does not prove a direct Chukchi Sea mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward northwestern Banning Lake approach
correspondence.finding: The western selected head occupies the small unnamed lake-and-stream terrain immediately northwest of Banning Lake. The original map shows the approach to Banning Lake’s northwestern arm among low ridges and small water bodies. The corridor is read at generalized scale; no name is inferred for the first feeder from the downstream Paliryuak identity.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Banning Lake passage and eastern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes southeast through the elongated Banning Lake setting and leaves its eastern end through the mapped small-lake and river outlet. It then turns northeast through the intervening channel network. Banning remains a lake component, not an alternative name assigned to the entire river system.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Western and central unnamed lake chain
correspondence.finding: East of Banning Lake, the selected corridor passes the smaller connected water bodies, enters the broad unnamed east–west lake marked D1 in the fish-resource annotation, and proceeds from its northeastern outlet through the connected northern and eastern lake reaches. The D1 prose explicitly places that unnamed lake on the Paliryuak River system; the observed lake shapes and inter-lake channels, rather than that basin statement alone, supply the route correspondence.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Northern inflows and eastern sheet-boundary connection
correspondence.finding: The northeastern middle lakes receive separately drawn northern inflows. The selected route follows the western incoming chain, then the eastward outlet across the adjoining77C/77D sheet boundary. Both sides show the inter-lake connection into the western arm of the lake locally named Merkley on77D. No northern feeder is substituted for the selected western approach.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Merkley and Surrey lake links
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor continues through the locally named Merkley Lake setting and its eastern/southeastern water connection into Surrey Lake. The original map shows Surrey Lake’s broad main water body, northern/lateral inflows and southward outlet arm. Those connections are directly read; the lake names are retained as component identities.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
mapped_component_names: Merkley Lake (source says locally known as)

correspondence.component_scope: Lower river and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: From the southern Surrey Lake arm the selected corridor follows the sinuous outlet river southeast and then east to its opening on the northwestern side of Wellington Bay. The original map labels this channel locally known as Paliryuak R.; its bounded fish-resource prose independently uses Paliryuak and places the fishery at the mouth. The mapped river opening and bay setting establish the terminal, rather than relying on the stored sea class. The Ekalluk outlet lies separately to the east.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
